previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of type 2 diabetes, kidney transplant, peripheral vascular disease, and prior toe amputations was admitted for fever and a chronic draining ulcer on his right fourth toe. Imaging revealed osteolysis suggestive of osteomyelitis. He underwent debridement and partial ostectomy of the infected bone. Initial broad-spectrum antibiotics were narrowed to ertapenem after wound cultures identified Citrobacter freundii, sensitive to most agents except Bactrim. A PICC line was placed for outpatient IV antibiotic therapy. His blood pressure was labile, prompting a switch from metoprolol to labetalol. Diabetes management was optimized with increased insulin dosing. Renal function remained stable, and he was discharged home with plans for weekly labs, infectious disease follow-up, and wound care.

in the appearance of the heart and lungs.

EXAMINATION:  RENAL TRANSPLANT U.S.

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with renal transplant now admitted with ___ //
eval for renal transplant abnormalities; measure resistive indices, etc

TECHNIQUE:  Grey scale as well as color and spectral Doppler ultrasound images
of the renal transplant were obtained.

COMPARISON:  ___

FINDINGS: 

The left iliac fossa transplant renal morphology is normal.  Specifically, the
cortex is of normal thickness and echogenicity, pyramids are normal, there is
no pelvi-infundibular thickening, and renal sinus fat is normal. There is no
hydronephrosis and no perinephric fluid collection.

The resistive index of intrarenal arteries ranges from 0.65 to 0.67, within
the normal range. Acceleration times and peak systolic velocities of the main
renal artery are normal. Vascularity is symmetric throughout transplant. The
transplant renal vein is patent and shows normal waveform.

IMPRESSION: 

Normal renal transplant ultrasound.
